purpose: Teach: 感傷/従順/習性/一服/四角い/極まりない/輝か/育む

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、卒業アルバム見て感傷的になってたな
lines.en: You got all sentimental looking at the yearbook, didn't you.
lines.style: Teasing but warm observation. Light, knowing tone. Accusatory in that affectionate way close friends use. Slight smile underneath.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、彼女に従順すぎないか?桜
lines.en: Aren't you a little too obedient to your girlfriend, Sakura?
lines.style: Dry counter-attack. Quick, self-protective deflection. Wry edge but no real bite. Testing her reaction.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、朝練サボる習性あるな
lines.en: You skip morning practice all the time, don't you.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact call-out. Light mockery, no malice. Watching him with amusement. Short, clipped delivery.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、ジュース一服しようぜ、桜
lines.en: Come on, let's grab some juice.
lines.style: Casual, inviting. Lightness returning to his voice. Shoulder-nudge energy. Genuine warmth without making it weird.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前ん家、四角い窓だらけだな
lines.en: Your place has nothing but square windows, doesn't it.
lines.style: Playful observation-turned-joke. Curious but amused tone. Like she's just noticed something silly about him. Slight laugh underneath.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、試験の前は緊張極まりないな、桜
lines.en: Before exams you get crazy tense, Sakura.
lines.style: Gentle ribbing disguised as casual comment. Knowing tone — he's noticed this pattern. Warm wryness, not mocking.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、合格して目が輝かれてたな
lines.en: Your eyes were shining when you passed, you know.
lines.style: Softer attack. Genuine compliment wrapped in her teasing tone so it doesn't feel too sincere. Slight smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、後輩を育む先輩だな、桜
lines.en: You're the kind of senior who really looks after the younger kids.
lines.style: Sincere admission, almost reluctant. Genuine praise breaking through his usual cool. Quiet, steady conviction underneath. Not overdoing it.
